segments: The seventeenth jubilee. Arab kings. Kaykaus, the ruler of the country of the Romans,
to rule over Aleppo,
because he saw that it was bereft of a master,
and that a nursing child was being proclaimed in it.
And his grandees advised him,
"This can be done easily,
if you take with you this al-Malik al-Afdal, son of Saladin, the lord of Samosata,
and show that on his account, wronged as he is by his brothers, you are acting with zeal,
to restore to him the kingdom of his father,
because he is the eldest son of Saladin."
And Sultan Izz al-Din sent and fetched al-Malik al-Afdal from Samosata,
and gave him gold, clothing, and an abundance of horses and weapons.
And he prepared him to go with him to Syria on the condition:
that Aleppo and everything adjacent to it should belong to al-Malik al-Afdal,
and any place they took from the dominion of al-Malik al-Ashraf in Mesopotamia should belong to Sultan Izz al-Din.
And they gathered armies and went first against Aintab and took it,
and it was handed over to al-Malik al-Afdal.
And they went from there to Tell Bashir,
and likewise took it.
And Sultan Izz al-Din took possession of it,
and did not give it to al-Malik al-Afdal.
And al-Afdal took offense,
and those who had surrendered it were also filled with remorse.
And from here treachery lurked in the heart of al-Afdal,
and he began to delay Izz al-Din from marching against Aleppo,
and said:
"First let us go and take Mabbugh and other places,
and then we shall be able to take Aleppo,
when it is left like a dove whose wings are plucked."
And when they went against Mabbugh,
Shihab al-Din the eunuch sent to al-Malik al-Ashraf,
and entreating him to come to the aid of the young child, his sister's son.
And al-Ashraf was moved with zeal, and came and encountered the army of the Romans at Mabbugh,
and the Romans were broken by him at the very beginning of the encounter.
And Sultan Izz al-Din held out no longer,
but abandoned everything and returned to his country.
And al-Ashraf went against Aintab and took it,
and likewise also Tell Bashir,
and gave them back to the lord of Aleppo.
Now those who surrendered Tell Bashir to al-Ashraf,
when they went to their country,
Sultan Izz
al-Din seized them,
and burned them pitilessly in a certain house.
And in that same year,
when the Franks were encamped,
as we have said,
against Damietta,
al-Malik al-Adil died on the seventh of the sixth month.
